ablation: real CoW anatomy vs. random same-size graph (12 nodes, 12 edges), B1 (graph injection only, no consistency loss), fold 0, seeds 0-2
motivation: Tests whether the SPECIFIC anatomical structure matters, or whether any graph of the same size would do -- the objection a sharp reviewer would raise about B1/B2's existing real-vs-no-graph comparison.
pre_registered: Descriptive comparison only (n=3 vs n=3 cannot support a real p<0.05 gate) -- reported honestly either way, not gated pass/fail. Documented in conversation before running.
finding: No measurable difference. Random-edge mean Dice (0.2263) is marginally HIGHER than real-anatomy mean Dice (0.2247); random-edge mean JDCR (0.9767) is marginally higher than real (0.9690). Both differences are well within seed-to-seed noise (SD ~0.001-0.002) and in any case not testable at n=3. The specific anatomical structure does not measurably help over an arbitrary graph of the same size, in this setup.
supporting_diagnostic: Cross-attention gate magnitudes (saved per checkpoint in training history) are tiny in BOTH arms, same order of magnitude: real B1's final gates were [-0.0029, -0.013, 0.0176]; random B1's were comparably small in every seed. The gate barely opens in either case, which is consistent with -- and likely explains -- why swapping the anatomy for a random graph makes almost no difference: very little information is flowing through the graph pathway regardless of what it's connected to.
implication: Strengthens the case that the bottleneck is HOW MUCH/WHAT information reaches the decoder via this pathway, not WHICH nodes it's wired to. Further graph-structure tweaks (edge design, different anatomical graphs) are unlikely to help; a pathway carrying genuinely new information (e.g. TopCoW/TopBrain-grounded vessel features, CLAUDE.md 2026-10) is the more promising remaining lever.
